title: [submit · L07] The two recalls, and the gap between them
body:
> **The submission desk for L07.** Post your solution here and a workflow replies
> within about a minute. One thread per lab, so the answers and the common mistakes accumulate
> where the next person will look.

**Lab:** 🟢 [`L07` — The two recalls, and the gap between them](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/labs/L07-two-recalls/brief.md) ·
20 min · track T4 (Testing)

> Recall@N and full-chain recall measure different stages. The gap between them is where the work is.

## Try it with nothing installed

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/akash-coded/nanorag?quickstart=1)

The container installs everything, checks your SQLite has FTS5, and opens the brief beside the
file you edit. Then:

```bash
python scripts/lab.py open L07
python scripts/lab.py run L07
python scripts/lab.py run L07 --hidden
```

In the editor, **Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+B** runs the lab whose file you have open.

## How to post

Paste your solution in a fenced ```` ```python ```` block. A reply arrives automatically with a
review.

**Say which decision you made.** Every lab's *Attribute* section asks you to commit to one before
writing code. If you chose differently from the reference, say so — that is more interesting than
agreeing, and it is the half of the lab that is not about typing.

## What the automatic review does, and does not

It reads your code with Python's **AST**. It checks the functions exist with the right names,
that you have not pasted the starter back, that nothing is hardcoded from the brief, and — for the
measurement tracks — that your write-up carries an interval rather than a point estimate.

**It does not run your code, deliberately.** Anyone can comment on a public discussion, and a
workflow that executes code from a comment is remote code execution on the runner. No amount of
permission tightening changes the fact that the code ran.

**For the real checks, including the hidden ones**, run them in a Codespace, or push and open a
pull request — [`labs.yml`](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/.github/workflows/labs.yml) evaluates the lab and
comments with a full result table.

## The gap between public and hidden checks is the lesson

Passing the public set and failing the hidden one is the normal experience. The hidden checks
cover what the brief deliberately did not mention — empty input, a duplicate id, a degenerate
config. **That gap is where the brief's assumptions were doing work you did not notice.**

## Stuck rather than submitting?

The [track thread for T4](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/discussions?discussions_q=label%3Alab) is the better place.
This one is for finished work.
